I'm going to be buying a touring bike at some point in the near future, and I have something very specific in mind. What I want to do is have 26" rims so I can have a larger selection of fatter tires and so that service will not be an issue pretty much anywhere I go in the world. I also want the frame to be built to accept disc brakes so that I can have a disc brake in the back and then mount a rim brake on the front fork instead of a disc brake. This way I have good stopping power in wet weather, but also have a normal rim brake to fall back on in case that's the only thing I can get parts and service for.

Other things I'm looking for are a weight no more than about 25 pounds when not loaded, definitely NOT carbon (that shit can't take abuse at all and it is expensive), fenders, and of course a set of racks for the front and back and enough room in the frame geometry so that I am not hitting the bags with my feet.

Do bikes like this exist or am I going to have to build one out of a mountain bike? I'd rather not do that.

edit: I think I've changed my mind. I'm still set on getting 26 inch rims, but I've decided to forgo getting a bike capable of handling disc brakes. A set of linear pull (aka direct pull) v brakes would give me plenty of stopping power while having the added bonus of being easy to service and get pads for pretty much anywhere in the world.

The Surly LHT frame can support linear pull v brakes and 26 inch rims, so that's my top candidate right now, but I'm open to cheaper, possibly more light weight choices if at all possible.

I think you could contact Surly and find weight, but their bikes are Chromoly, which does give the best strength/weight ratio (my opinion). It's unlikely that you'll break the frame; there are others (more expensive), jonesbikes.com (designed to give you some flexibility in the frame), which are also either chromoly or titanium; finally, there is bikesdirect.com, which has a bike known as the "9iron elite;" it's not listed on their catalog site, but they tell me that they have all sizes. BE CAREFUL if you choose that last option. I bought one, and it was much too large, although the listed sizes were my size. The problem of fitting, for me, came down to the length of top tube, and their XL size is 24.5 inches top tube. They also list the standover height incorrectly (which is why I made my mistake); so you need to look at the listed measurements very carefully. The most important thing in any bike is fit. If the bike doesn't fit you, you will be sorry you bought it, no matter how nice it is. By contrast, if the bike fits you, you will love it and keep it forever (my Gary Fisher); even if you modify it (which I have done), it will still be a dear friend, and you will regret the day you sell it or it breaks. I hope you find exactly what you want. IF you want to see what others ride, go to www.crazyguyonabike.com to see what folks ride. They have a section called "loaded bicycles" that will show you specifically what people have used to ride across country and around the world. It's my ambition to go myself.
At present, I ride a recumbent quite a bit, so there's also that (mine is a TourEasy). Hope you find exactly what works for you.
